newsitem.title: INDIA: Israel says ready for free trade pact with India. [CORRECTED 08:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israel says ready for free trade pact with India. [CORRECTED 08:10 GMT]

text.p: Israel is ready to discuss a free trade agreement with India to boost business ties, an Israeli foreign ministry offical said in New Delhi on Tuesday.

"We are ready to negotiate a free trade agreement with India on the same level of pacts we have with the United States, Canada and the European Union," said Itzhak Shelef, the Israeli foreign ministry's deputy director general, Asia and Pacific.
Israeli officials said Shelef was due to meet Indian foreign ministry officials to prepare for the first visit to India by Israeli President Ezer Weizman, expected later this year.
Shelef told reporters that trade between the two countries had increased steadily after they established diplomatic ties in 1992.
Trade between India and Israel stood at $600 million in 1995, with Israel's export share at $350 million, an Israeli diplomat said.
India established diplomatic ties with Israel in January 1992, a few days after Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat visited New Delhi, apparently clearing the move.
It was not immediately clear how India would respond to a free trade agreement with Israel.
(Corrects to delete reference to trade group)
Shelef said his talks in New Delhi would also take up regional issues, including Afghanistan.
"We want a peaceful, negotiated settlement in Afghanistan," he said.
